codeSnippets.output: A card that re-themes everywhere the moment --main-color changes.
Derived sizes computed from one base spacing variable.

exercise.instruction: Define two variables in :root: --main-color: #6366f1 and --spacing: 16px. Then on .card apply background: var(--main-color) and padding: var(--spacing), and give the h2 color: var(--main-color) so it matches the card.
exercise.starterCode:
Branded Card

Its background, padding, and heading color all come from one source of truth.

Second Card

Change --main-color in :root and every card updates at once.
hints: Hint 3: h2 { color: var(--main-color); } — try editing the variable to see every use change.

quiz.question: Where do you define global CSS variables?
options: in :root so they cascade to everything

quiz.question: What does var(--brand, red) do if --brand is undefined?
options: it uses the fallback value red

quiz.question: CSS variables are great for theming because...
options: redefining a variable in a scope updates every place that uses it at once
they make CSS run faster than hardcoded values
they let you write JavaScript in stylesheets
